newsitem.title: USA: Prime Capital sues seeking $6.3 million.
newsitem.headline: Prime Capital sues seeking $6.3 million.

text.p: Prime Capital Corp, which provides financing for health companies, said Monday its Prime Leasing Inc unit filed a federal lawsuit in Northern Illinois alleging that several lessees are in default of their leases.
The lawsuit seeks rental payments, late charges and interest in an amount not less than $6.3 million, the company said in a news release.

The suit also seeks to enforce certain guarantees by individual defendants of the obligations of the lessees under the equipment leases; alleges a breach of the Illinois Consumer Fraud and Deceptive Business Practices Act by the corporate defendants and an individual defendant; and also alleges a conspiracy to violate the act by the corporate defendants and two individual defendants, the company said.

Of the $6.3 million of equipment leases, $1.8 million are owned by Prime and the remainder have been transferred and assigned by Prime to special purpose corporations participating in certain equipment securitization programs.
The defaults and violations alleged in the suit may require Prime to repurchase such assigned leases from these special purpose corporations, the company said.

The company said it will be unable to ascertain if it will ultimately suffer any losses as a result of the defaults and violations alleged in the suit until it can ascertain the magnitude of the defaults and violations or the extent of recovery pursuant to this litigation.
The company also said its primary lenders have been advised of the occurrence of such defaults and violations and are continuing to provide financing to the company.
Prime Capital shares closed down 1/4 at 6-1/2 Monday.
